content:
Siri AI is a major upgrade for Apple's assistant and is now available on iOS 27. I noticed a prominent difference between it and other AI assistants, and it's a good one.

The all-new Siri on iOS 27 doesn't pretend to be human, unlike other AI chatbots

I've been using Siri AI for nearly four months since the first iOS 27 Beta was released. Overall, it has met all my expectations.

The all-new Siri is far more powerful than the previous generation, truly delivering on its original promise of becoming a truly useful assistant on Apple devices.

However, I have to admit: if you need the most advanced and powerful AI tools on the market, competitors like ChatGPT, Claude, and Google Gemini might be a better fit for you.

That said, after using Siri AI and comparing it with those third-party tools, I noticed a key difference that makes me clearly lean towards Siri.

Unlike other AI chatbots, Siri doesn't pretend to be human.

It doesn't go on at length, nor does it mimic human personality, leading you to不知不觉 build a personal relationship with it.

Siri is practical, smart, and flexible, doing what you ask it to do. But the way it responds clearly shows it's a tool, not a person. It often reminds you it's an AI and may make mistakes. It also doesn't pretend to go on a date with you.

In contrast, ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are full of personality and stance, showing more human-like traits, but to me, that feeling doesn't seem very authentic.

I know some users like this more 'humanised' approach. But I'd rather AI assistants just do their job instead of pretending to be something else.

AI is changing the world. But AI chatbots are tools, not people. Apple understands this and has built the all-new Siri on this foundation, which I greatly appreciate.

What do you think about how 'human-like' AI assistants should be? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
